Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Navigation Warning?

In this glossary, Navigation Warning refers to: Official broadcast of hazards, obstructions, or operational restrictions that may affect safe navigation.

How is Navigation Warning used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "All vessels, navigation warning: unlit wreck reported near buoy Lima, position 51°13.4′ N 001°22.8′ E."

Why does Navigation Warning matter in maritime?

Navigation Warning matters because it supports clear communication in External Communication contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Navigation Warning?

Navigation Warning is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Navigation Warning belong to?

In this glossary, Navigation Warning is grouped under External Communication. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

Official broadcast of hazards, obstructions, or operational restrictions that may affect safe navigation.

Operational example

All vessels, navigation warning: unlit wreck reported near buoy Lima, position five one degrees one three decimal four minutes north, zero zero one degrees two two decimal eight minutes east.
